seal.statement: The owner asked (2026-09-18) for a proper installation package for a newly registered lab worker, so everything it needs is installed in one go by one script that can be copied to the worker and run there. Fleet discovery reports what a worker lacks, but nothing installed it: both current workers still miss helm and wasm-tools, one also psql and the pinned MovieLens dataset, and each gap turns into files that red there and are run again on the controller. `node scripts/lab.js provision` now writes that script, and `--copy NODE` puts it in a registered worker's home directory and prints the one command to run. The toolchain it installs is not written down a second time: it is the full-corpus canary's own install steps, taken from the workflow when the script is generated, so a worker and CI cannot drift apart. Around them the script checks the machine can be provisioned before asking for anything, installs the system packages a worker needs (git, a C++ toolchain for native modules, docker), node at the engines floor through a digest-pinned nvm, the checkout (cloned, or brought to main when clean) with dependencies that match its lockfile, the controller's public key for ssh, and ends by printing what the worker now has. Discovery now also checks java, ripgrep and jq, which the canary installs and some files need.

text: `node scripts/lab.js provision [--output FILE] [--copy NAME]` generates the worker setup (scripts/lab/probe.js workerSetupScript, workerCloneUrl, copyWorkerSetup; scripts/lab/lagrange-lab.js commandProvision). The script embeds the full-corpus canary's "Install gate CLI tools" and "Fetch MovieLens dataset (digest-pinned)" steps line for line, read from the workflow at generation time, and around them: refusal of non-Linux, non-x86_64, apt-less and root machines before sudo is asked; system packages a hosted runner already has (git, ca-certificates, curl, build-essential, python3, unzip, docker.io only when docker is absent) and the docker group; node at the engines floor through a digest-pinned nvm v0.40.3 installer; the checkout cloned over https or brought to main when clean (fast-forward on a branch, detach otherwise); npm ci only when node_modules does not match the lockfile (the probe's own check); the dataset only when its digest is wrong; the public halves of the identities ssh offers from the controller; a report of what the worker has. Discovery now also checks java, rg and jq (gaps, not disqualifiers). --copy uses bounded scp and prints the command; nothing is run remotely. docs/development/home-lab.md gains the section. Verified end to end: the generated script ran in a fresh ubuntu:22.04 container (the base of the lab workers' Mint 21.3) as a sudo-capable non-root user and installed everything, reporting node v22.23.2, helm v3.16.3, wasm-tools 1.236.0, psql 14, java 11, ripgrep 13, jq 1.6, g++ 11, docker 29 and the dataset digest ok; a second run succeeded unchanged.

Round 1 approve, no blocking findings. All required checks green (eslint, literals 0 new, complexity 1819/1819, cognitive 160/160, audit:shards, test:unused:push, harness 5/5, probe done, seal current). Independent ubuntu:22.04 container run closer to a real worker (password sudo through a pty, existing nvm 0.39.3 with default 22.12.0, a detached older checkout with its node_modules, an existing authorized key, USER unset): two runs exit 0, sudo asked once each, node 22.23.2 installed and used, checkout moved to 7e4f223ff, npm ci correctly skipped, dataset fetched and checked, second run changed nothing and duplicated no key. Quoting of URL, keys, floor and digests via shellQuote holds against hostile comments; canary text is subshell-contained; refusal ordering modifies nothing before sudo; checkout logic behaves on behind/diverged/dirty/unrelated repos; canary toolchain equals ci.yml's but for a version print. 25 mutations, all receipt claims red. Non-blocking: shellQuote on key comments unwitnessed; canary step shapes the worker cannot reproduce (${{ }}, GITHUB_*, env:, shell:, working-directory:) would be embedded and fail only at runtime; set +u around nvm, the dirty guard and the nvm digest check unwitnessed; checkout edges (a clean non-main branch fast-forwarded, a detached HEAD with local commits moved silently, an unrelated detached repo switched); a cosmetic redirect error on first run; the canary step re-runs every time; the report's tool list is a second list; a stale corpusReadiness docstring; --copy silently wins over --output; scp has no ServerAlive; no -- before REPO_URL.

Round-1 non-blocking items taken. Generation refuses a canary step a worker cannot reproduce (a ${{ }} expression, a GITHUB_* or RUNNER_* variable other than RUNNER_TEMP, a step env, shell or working-directory) instead of writing a script that fails after sudo. The checkout moves only when nothing is lost: main fast-forwards; a detached HEAD follows main only when main contains it; any other branch, local commits or local changes are left alone with a message; clone and fetch take -- before the URL. The report is built from WORKER_TOOL_SOURCES, which now carries each tool's version command, so it cannot drift from what discovery checks. The dataset digest reads no longer print a redirect error on first run. --copy with --output is refused. scp gets the ServerAlive bounds. The header says the canary toolchain is re-applied. corpusReadiness docstring updated. Witnesses: six unreproducible step shapes refused; a hostile key comment executed twice in a sandbox HOME is appended verbatim once and runs nothing; set +u around nvm and the installer digest check before its execution; a new test runs the checkout block against five local repos (main behind, dirty, other branch, detached behind, detached with a local commit); every checked tool is reported by its own version command; --copy with --output refused. 7 mutations of these, all red; harness 6/6.

Round 2 reject, one blocking finding: the new checkout test ran git with the inherited environment (its git() helper and the block runner), so inside a push hook from a linked worktree - where git exports an absolute GIT_DIR and the corpus gate re-runs with process.env - it would commit into, clone from and detach the pusher's repository; reproduced by aiming GIT_DIR at a throwaway repo, which got a commit. Everything else green: 16/16 tests, eslint, literals, 1819/1819, 160/160, audit:shards, unused, harness 6/6, probe done, seal current; round-1 items verified; 17 mutations, 13 red (survivors: -- before the URL twice, the redirect form, --ff-only on main); container run after the measurement: two runs exit 0 with one sudo prompt, detached checkout moved to main, npm ci skipped, dataset fetched with no redirect error, all 9 tools reported, second run changed nothing; the checkout block against real GitHub main left a detached local commit, a topic branch and main with a local commit alone. Non-blocking: job- and workflow-level variables are not refused; a message said "not behind" for a branch that is behind.

Round-2 repairs. Every git the provisioning tests run - the checkout test's helper and block runner, the key-block run and the provision CLI spawns - uses gitProcessEnvironment() (scripts/checks/git-process-environment.js), and the provision command's own git reads pass it too. The checkout test now sets GIT_DIR to a decoy repository for its duration and asserts the decoy got no commit; it also covers main with a local commit (left alone, never merged), pinning --ff-only. Generation refuses a canary step that references a variable its job or workflow defines (a worker's shell does not have it). The left-alone messages now say what was found. The same GIT_DIR flaw was fixed in test-placement's tests in its own worktree. Mutations: the inherited git env in either place and dropping the job-variable refusal all go red; all test files pass with GIT_DIR=/nonexistent-decoy.

Round 3 approve, no blocking findings. The GIT_DIR fix holds: the three test files pass 16/16 normally, with GIT_DIR=/nonexistent-decoy, with GIT_DIR at the absolute path of a throwaway repo as a linked-worktree hook exports it, and with GIT_DIR, GIT_WORK_TREE and GIT_INDEX_FILE all aimed at it; the throwaway repo gained nothing. The decoy witness goes red when either env fix is reverted. Job- and workflow-level variable refusal and the main-with-local-commit case verified (red under their mutations); messages checked against local repos; the generated script is otherwise byte-identical to the round-2 container-tested one. All required checks green (eslint, literals, 1819/1819, 160/160, audit:shards, unused, harness 6/6, probe done, seal current). Non-blocking: the decoy is installed after the upstream's first commit (a reverted helper would still reach the real GIT_DIR once, though the test goes red); survivors: the provision command's own gitEnv (read-only), workflow-level env refusal untested, -- before the URL and the redirect form.
